text:
Maya Patel: FYI seeing repeated RX/TX errors and interface flaps on g5n.12xlarge nodes in us-east-1a. Packet loss spikes east-west between inference pools. Logs attached below.

Liam O'Connor: :eyes: started looking. Any pattern on kernel/driver versions?

Maya Patel: All affected are running ami-rl-infer-202601 with kernel 5.15. ena 3.10. Firmware reported as ENA fw v2.0.4 in dmesg.

Sasha Kim: Here's snippet from dmesg from node ip-10-1-5-23:
```
[  123.456789] ena: enp1s0: firmware assert at 0x1a2b
[  123.456793] ena: enp1s0: Rx errors: 1248 Tx errors: 12
[  123.456800] IPv4: dropping packet, mtu mismatch
```

Maya Patel: We also see MTU mismatch warnings when jumbo frames enabled (mtu 9000). When we drop to 1500 flaps drop to almost zero.

Liam O'Connor: Could be ENA fw/driver mismatch or a RoCE/RDMA interaction. Any RDMA configured on these instances?

Maya Patel: No explicit RDMA, but some clients enable RoCE for vec-scatter jobs. Not peak usage though.

Sasha Kim: Quick checks I ran:
- ethtool -S enp1s0 shows large rx_csum_errors and rx_over_errors
- ifdown/ifup recovers for ~10-20m then flaps again

Liam O'Connor: Workaround idea: roll nodes to kernel 6.1 + ena 3.14 or pin MTU to 1500 and disable tso/gro on enp1s0.
Command we tested:
```
sudo ip link set dev enp1s0 mtu 1500
sudo ethtool -K enp1s0 tso off gso off gro off
```
Result: no flaps in 2h on canary group (5 nodes).

Maya Patel: Filed ticket with AWS NFW-12345 with logs and dmesg. Provider asked for ena fw dump and pcap of east-west traffic.

infra-bot: Deploy check: canary group rollback scheduled if any node reports >5 flaps in 1h :rotating_light:

Sasha Kim: Recommend next steps:
1) Expand canary to 20 nodes in us-east-1a with MTU 1500 + tso/gro off
2) Collect ena fw dumps (ena_tool) and pcap over 30m
3) Schedule maintenance window to test kernel 6.1+ena 3.14

Liam O'Connor: Also add automatic routing fallback in routing policy to route latency-sensitive requests to us-east-1b if packet loss >1%.

Maya Patel: I'll update the incident ticket and add a quick runbook in /runbooks/eng-infra/nic-flaps.md. Thx everyone. :thumbsup:
